references.text: Laws about taking a cloak as collateral that must be returned before sunset, because it is the poor person's only covering - the same principle of not taking essential items as collateral
Detailed laws about collateral, including the prohibition against entering a person's house to seize collateral and the requirement to return collateral to the poor before nightfall
Prohibition against taking a widow's clothing as collateral - part of the same legal collection concerning the protection of vulnerable people's essential belongings
Job describes the wicked who take millstones as collateral from the poor, a violation of this prohibition
Job's complaint about those who seize collateral from widows and orphans, related to the abuse of collateral rules
Amos condemns those who lie on pledged clothing at the altar - criticism of unjust collateral practices
Ezekiel describes the righteous person who returns collateral to the debtor, in accordance with the laws about collateral
Ezekiel describes the wicked person who does not return collateral, a violation of the collateral laws
